questions.question: PR #1197 round 3: the `source` check only tests that each declared member occurs in its source. A new Environment row (E16, which O21/O44 propose for the reopen) passes D19 and D34 with no row for it. How should this close?

options.label: Opt-in reverse check (Recommended)
options.description: A source entry may set `complete = true`: every row of that source column must then be matched by a member. Set it on the Environment sources of D19 and D34 (D34's D9 source excludes Found(e, item), so the reverse check can't be the default). Behaviour change, with a test seen failing first.

options.label: Reverse check by default
options.description: Every source row must be matched, unless a new `uncovered` list exempts it. Stricter, but D34 then needs an exemption for Found(e, item), and every future source pays the same cost.

options.label: Narrow the docstring only
options.description: State in the Bound that a source element no member names goes unreported, and file the reverse check. The E16 case stays a false pass until then.

questions.question: Spec mode on the real `sdd/specs/052-store-key.md` exits 1 permanently: its sentence 'KEY-006, KEY-007 and KEY-A-01 are unassigned' names retired IDs, and no declaration can silence that. What should the fix be?

options.label: Add `retired` to [[ids]] (Recommended)
options.description: [[ids]] gains an optional `retired` list: IDs the document names but deliberately never defines. They aren't reported as citations, and naming one that is defined is a finding. Small change, tested on a 052-shaped fixture.

options.label: File it to BK-506
options.description: Leave spec mode as is and record the limit in the docstring. BK-506 runs G3 on a spec first, so it decides how retired IDs are declared.

questions.question: The six OP-01 mutant tests depend on exact cells of the live record ('8 rows' for D41, D18's Closed row, D19's 'E6, E15 (O3)'), cells the OP-01 reopen is invited to change. The armed reopen session can't edit tests, so its record-only commit would turn tooling-tests red. How should this close?

options.label: Derive targets from the parse (Recommended)
options.description: Keep running the mutants on the real record and its real sidecar (ADR-0045's 'real record'), but compute each target from the parsed document (D41's row count, D18's last row, a D19 key cell, a D9 row) instead of a literal. They survive a reopen that adds rows or columns.

options.label: Frozen copy beside the tests
options.description: Commit a fixture copy of OP-01 and its sidecar under tests/. Stable forever, but the mutants no longer show the check can fail on the record it actually guards.

options.label: File it
options.description: Leave the tests as they are; the reopen PR updates them in a non-armed session. CI goes red there until it does.

questions.question: `/observe-review` step 5 says the freeze tag is `observe/<entry>/freeze-<n>` with `<n>` 'one past the last', and RFC-0029 R2 only says 'the next freeze takes n + 1'. What should a first freeze (OP-01's, which BK-506 pre-registers on) be numbered?

options.label: freeze-1 (Recommended)
options.description: Skill says '`<n>` 1 for the entry's first freeze, else one past the last'. Counts freezes from one, and the RFC's 'n + 1' reads naturally.

options.label: freeze-0
options.description: Skill says '`<n>` 0 for the first'. Zero-based, so freeze-1 is the first reopen's freeze.

questions.question: PR #1197 has reached /ship's soft ceiling of 5 finding-rounds. Findings per round: 3, 4, 11, 9 (8 fixed, 1 refuted), and now 7. Severity has fallen: round 3 had false passes the OP-01 reopen would hit, and round 4 a zero-padding bug that broke spec mode. Round 5 has nothing that changes a result on OP-01 or on the real specs 052 and 045 (both exit 0). Every subject row is covered, every mutant fails its check when it is disabled, and CI is green. Round 5's 7 findings are latent or about wording: (1) D38's source isn't marked complete; (2) the docstring doesn't say row citations by name ("D34's changed row") go unchecked; (3) the docstring says full-form ranges (OP-01/E1 to OP-01/E3) expand, and they don't; (4) the sidecar's short form D also catches "RFC-0024 D5"; (5) G3's "fix the sidecar" would hide a duplicated heading ID; (6) the test comment still claims a full enumeration; (7) members written in full form plus a short-form source cell give a false finding. How should the loop continue?

options.label: Narrow, file, verify once (Recommended)
options.description: Fix 1 to 6 with no new code: narrow the docstring and comments to what the code does, mark D38's source complete (no finding changes today), note the D short form in the sidecar, and limit G3's 'fix the sidecar' to declarations found wrong on re-reading. Narrow 7 in the docstring too (members and source written in the same form). File full-form ranges and full-form member matching as one new backlog item. Then one closing panel (unprimed, whole-file, measuring) on a text-only fix pass.

options.label: Fix all in code, verify once
options.description: Also fix 3 and 7 in code: expand full-form ranges, and compare IDs in one canonical form rather than as written. No new backlog item. Then the same closing panel. More code means more for that panel to find, so it may not close cleanly.

options.label: Waive and close now
options.description: File all 7 as one backlog item and close on the current head without another fix pass. That needs your waiver, because the stop rule forbids ending on a round with must-fix findings. Points 2, 3 and 6 leave false or overreaching statements in the shipped docstring and comment.
